thread:
cobalt_svc: Hi Redwood — we're seeing a spike in KMS decrypts tied to our dedicated deployment (key: projects/customer-789/locations/global/keys/ch-cobalt). Not sure what triggered it, looks like 03:11-03:15Z. Can you confirm and advise?

sara_support: Thanks for flagging — we got this. Can you paste the exact key resource and any suspected IPs? We'll triage immediately.

cobalt_svc: Key resource above. No IP yet, customer noticed increased outbound traffic to api.redwood.example and some unexpected model responses.

aj_security: @sara_support putting this to high priority. Mike oncall, can you take containment? We should assume potential unauthorized access to the key until proven otherwise.

mike_oncall: On it. Steps I'm planning: 1) Pull KMS audit entries (decrypts) 2) Identify principals (svcacct / iam user) 3) Temporarily restrict key usage via a deny policy / key-binding change 4) Rotate the key if we see unapproved principals.

tom_platform: I'll run the audit query now. Sample CloudTrail/Stackdriver query I'll use:

```
resource.type=\"kms_key\"
protoPayload.methodName:\"Decrypt\"
resource.labels.key_id:\"ch-cobalt\"
timestamp>=\"2026-06-15T03:00:00Z\"
```

tom_platform: Also grabbing recent deployment events and RBAC changes across the tenant.

auditbot: Search complete — 7 Decrypt events found between 2026-06-15T03:09:22Z and 2026-06-15T03:14:58Z. Principals: serviceAccount:cobalt-worker@cust-789.iam.gserviceaccount.com (5), user:devops@cobalthealth.com (2).

aj_security: Interesting — service account has 5 decrypts. Did the customer recently onboard a batch job? @cobalt_svc can you confirm whether cobalt-worker should have key access?

cobalt_svc: No, we rotated off cobalt-worker weeks ago. That service account should be disabled. We'll check internally but looks suspicious.

sara_support: For containment we can: 1) add a temporary KMS deny for cobalt-worker 2) add a Key policy requiring requesting principal to be in a verified group 3) ask customer to rotate any downstream credentials. We need approval to apply deny now.

mike_oncall: Approve the deny. Apply it as a short-lived change and capture rollback steps. I'll also block egress to api.redwood.example for that tenant subnet as a precaution.

aj_security: tom, pull the RBAC audit for IAM modifications in the last 30 days and any service account key creates. Use this query:

```
logName:\"projects/cust-789/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity\"
protoPayload.methodName:(\"SetIamPolicy\" OR \"CreateServiceAccountKey\")
resource.labels.project_id:\"cust-789\"
timestamp>=\"2026-05-15T00:00:00Z\"
```

tom_platform: Running now. Also collecting VPC flow logs for 03:00-03:20Z.

auditbot: RBAC search results: 1 SetIamPolicy by user:platform-admin@cobalthealth.com on 2026-05-20T14:02Z, no SA key creates found in the last 30 days.

aj_security: No obvious recent SA key creation. Could be a compromised platform-admin. We'll need the customer's assurance and a forensics window.

sara_support: I've opened internal ticket INC-2026-0615 and invited SRE+Sec. Notifying the customer with next steps: temporary deny applied, key access restricted, we will provide full export of decrypt events.

cobalt_svc: Thanks. We will look for any internal credential issues. Can you also provide the last 10 model calls that used that key (request ids)? We need them for our legal team.

tom_platform: I can export the request ids and associated request metadata. Example export format: `[{request_id, principal, method, timestamp, src_ip}]`. Will share secure artifact.

mike_oncall: Containment done: applied deny rule for serviceAccount:cobalt-worker@cust-789. Blocked suspected egress flows. Rotating key is queued — awaiting customer confirmation.

aj_security: Next steps: 1) full audit export to customer 2) customer to confirm rotation and internal remediation 3) optional full key rotation if customer requests 4) post-incident review to update onboarding/deprovisioning checklist.

sara_support: Update to customer sent. I'll post the export link once ready. @aj_security please prepare note for postmortem.

cobalt_svc: Received. Appreciate the quick action. We'll confirm internal deprovisioning and reply within 2 hours.

mike_oncall: Follow-up: logs show 2 decrypts by user:devops@cobalthealth.com came from a CI agent IP 34.120.55.66. We're sharing details in the ticket.

sara_support: Thanks. Locking thread for major updates — will keep posting concise updates in the ticket. :lock:

aj_security: Assigned post-incident owner: @aj_security. We'll schedule a blameless postmortem after containment + customer confirmation.

sara_support: Confirmed last_message. Will update INC-2026-0615 with final exports and timeline.
